label: sequence contains y/s/1 (or 0/d) earlier: dense memory-of-token feature
explanation: Dense feature (42% of steps, 99% of sequences). Most activation mass sits in sequences where one of y, s, 1 (and more weakly 0, d) has already been input: it switches on after such a token appears in the original phase and stays on through <DEL> and the copy phase. When one of these tokens is the current output it fires almost always (out_tok y 99%, s 96%, 1 95%, d/0 80%). The largest activations (top ~6.5) come from sequences starting with y/s/1, peaking on an o input in the original phase and on <DEL> and the first copy steps. In the copy phase it tends to die out once the last pending y/s/1 has been output, but encoding that explicitly did not beat plain seen(). It also gives weak diffuse activations (bottom quartiles, often <0.1 of max) in sequences without these tokens, often on o inputs, and these cause most of the recall gap. Predicate dev scores: P 0.55, R 0.70, F1 0.62, mass recall 0.87.
